order_description: Implantation of a hypoglossal nerve neurostimulator system (stimulation lead, pulse generator and respiratory sensor) for obstructive sleep apnea

selection_reason: The order is for hypoglossal nerve stimulator implantation for obstructive sleep apnea, and L38398 is a Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for OSA LCD whose background matches the three-component FDA-approved system (stimulation lead, breathing sensor lead, generator) named in the order. L38307 is the same policy from another contractor and equally covers the order; L38528 describes a similar system but is also the same policy title, so any of the three could apply. The patient is a Medicare beneficiary per the record, and the chart documents severe OSA (AHI 32), CPAP intolerance, and a sleep medicine and otolaryngology evaluation, consistent with the typical criteria for this LCD.

criteria.policy_text: Beneficiary is 22 years of age or older
criteria.explanation: The sleep medicine note of 2026-03-06 and the otolaryngology note of 2026-03-31 both record the patient as 35 years old, which is above the 22-year minimum.

criteria.policy_text: Body mass index (BMI) is less than 35 kg/m2
criteria.explanation: BMI was 29.5 kg/m2 on 2026-03-31 (R48, also documented in R82) and 29.06 kg/m2 on 2025-01-22 (R47). Both are below 35.

criteria.policy_text: A polysomnography (PSG) is performed within 24 months of first consultation for HGNS implant
criteria.explanation: Attended in-laboratory PSG was performed on 2025-11-03 (R24, report R76). The first HGNS consultation was on 2026-03-06 (R25). The PSG falls well within 24 months before that consultation.

criteria.policy_text: Beneficiary has predominantly obstructive events (defined as central and mixed apneas less than 25% of the total AHI)
criteria.explanation: The PSG report labels the sleep apnea as obstructive (R76), but it gives no count or percentage of central or mixed apneas. The record therefore cannot show that central and mixed apneas are below 25% of the AHI.

criteria.policy_text: AHI is 15 to 65 events per hour
criteria.explanation: AHI was 32 events/hour on the 2025-11-04 PSG (R42, R76), which is within the 15 to 65 range.

criteria.policy_text: Documentation of CPAP failure (AHI greater than 15 despite CPAP usage) or CPAP intolerance (less than 4 hours per night, 5 nights per week, or the CPAP has been returned), including shared decision making that the patient was intolerant of CPAP despite consultation with a sleep expert
criteria.explanation: The alternative used is CPAP intolerance. The device download shows CPAP use on only 11 of the last 30 nights (R50), averaging 2.8 hours on nights used (R43), which is below the 4 hours per night and 5 nights per week thresholds. The sleep medicine physician, a sleep expert, documented a shared decision making conversation with the patient about the CPAP trial and alternatives, and recorded that the patient is intolerant of CPAP despite mask and pressure changes (R81). The otolaryngologist confirmed this (R82).

criteria.policy_text: Absence of complete concentric collapse at the soft palate level as seen on a drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) procedure
criteria.explanation: The DISE report of 2026-04-27 documents partial anteroposterior collapse at the soft palate and explicitly states no complete concentric collapse (R77). The DISE procedure is recorded in R27 and R41.

criteria.policy_text: No other anatomical findings that would compromise performance of device (e.g., tonsil size 3 or 4 per standardized tonsillar hypertrophy grading scale)
criteria.explanation: Tonsils are documented as size 1 on the Brodsky scale, and Mallampati class is II (R82). The DISE shows partial collapses at the oropharynx, tongue base and velum with no epiglottic collapse (R77). No documented anatomical finding is recorded as compromising the device.

criteria.policy_text: HGNS is not medically reasonable and necessary when any listed contraindication is present, including central and mixed apneas making up more than one-quarter of the total AHI, implanted devices, BMI of 35 or more, neuromuscular disease, hypoglossal-nerve palsy, severe pulmonary disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension, severe valvular heart disease, NYHA class III or IV heart failure, recent MI or severe arrhythmia, uncontrolled hypertension, serious mental illness, other sleep disorders, pregnancy, MRI needs, inability to operate the remote, or conditions affecting neurological control of the upper airway
criteria.explanation: The otolaryngology contraindication screen (R82) documents that none of the listed contraindications is present, and that the patient has no implanted devices, is able to operate the remote, and has no anticipated MRI need. BMI is 29.5 (R48). The one contraindication not resolved is central and mixed apneas exceeding one-quarter of the AHI, which the PSG report does not quantify (R76). The most recent blood pressure in the record is from 2025-01-22 (R44), and R82 says blood pressure is controlled, so that check relies on the screen rather than a current measurement. R19 is a home CPAP unit, which is not an implanted device.

decision_explanation: Criteria 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 are met. Covered Indications.4 is insufficient because the record gives no central or mixed apnea count or percentage, so the required predominantly obstructive threshold of under 25% cannot be verified. The related contraindication limitation (Limitations.3) is also insufficient for the same reason. No criterion is clearly unmet, so the coverage decision cannot be made until the central and mixed apnea proportion of the AHI is documented.
